mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where FEDFUNDS has declined over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 2.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which reduces equity valuations and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where CPIAUCSL yoy change exceeds 2.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.5%) indicate a tight labor market and aggressive monetary tightening, which suppresses corporate earnings growth and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with monetary tightening
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in periods meeting the trigger condition, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months indicates a strengthening labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where PAYEMS has increased over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A three-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.5 percentage points indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate profits, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where UNRATE has increased by more than 0.5 percentage points over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions, a decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening demand for residential construction, which typically precedes a slowdown in overall economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in late-cycle expansions when HOUST declines, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window within late-cycle periods.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deceleration in real GDP growth (GDPC1) and decline in retail sales (RSAFS) over the past three months indicate a broad-based economic slowdown, reducing corporate earnings expectations and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where both GDPC1 and RSAFS have declined over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A three-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates weakening manufacturing activity and reduced economic output, which typically leads to lower corporate profits and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) in periods where INDPRO has declined over the prior 3 months, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
